scenes.title: Why GPUs spend 90% of their time waiting

beats.say: A modern AI GPU can crunch nearly a quadrillion operations per second — yet during standard attention, its cores spend ninety percent of their time starving for data. FlashAttention shatters that memory wall without changing a single decimal place of the math.

scenes.title: The GPU memory hierarchy and Roofline wall

beats.say: Inside an NVIDIA H100, compute and memory live in different universes. Tensor cores roar at nine hundred eighty-nine teraflops, while off-chip HBM feeds them at just three point three five terabytes per second. Right beside the cores sits tiny on-chip SRAM — six times faster, at nineteen terabytes per second, yet only fifty megabytes large.

Plot that gap on a Roofline chart. To saturate the chip, every byte loaded from HBM needs nearly three hundred math operations. Standard attention writes and reloads the entire N by N score matrix across HBM at every step — pinning your GPU deep inside the memory-bound valley.

scenes.title: Tiling the attention landscape inside SRAM

beats.say: FlashAttention asks one ruthless question: why ever materialize the N by N attention matrix in HBM at all? Instead, it slices Queries, Keys, and Values into compact blocks that fit completely inside blazing on-chip SRAM.

One block of queries stays pinned in SRAM while blocks of keys and values stream past. Each tile computes local scores, folds them into the running output on-chip, and discards the intermediate block immediately. Total HBM traffic plunges by an order of magnitude — from N squared down to N squared d over M.

scenes.title: Exact online softmax without seeing the full row

beats.say: There is one subtle catch: softmax normally needs the maximum and total sum across an entire row before normalizing a single weight. How can you compute exact softmax when you only see one tiny tile at a time?

The secret is online softmax. As each tile arrives, track the running maximum and running denominator. Whenever a larger score appears, multiply the old sum and output by an exact exponential correction factor. By the final tile, the tiled result matches full softmax to machine precision — with zero approximation.

scenes.title: Don't write what you can fuse

beats.say: By fusing matrix multiply, softmax, and dropout into one SRAM kernel, FlashAttention runs two to four times faster and unlocks million-token context windows with exact math. When compute outruns memory, the golden rule of GPU engineering is simple: don't write what you can fuse.
